Situation1: They occasionally ask their parents if everything is going well at home.
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: Your friend calls, sounding very upset, and asks if you have a moment to talk about a recent argument with their partner.
Story: I was sitting at the kitchen table, sipping tea with my mom, when I noticed the tired lines on her face. Dad was unusually quiet, and I could sense something was off. Remembering how important it is to check in, I gently asked, “Is everything okay at home?” Mom hesitated, then started to open up about some worries she had about Dad’s health. I nodded, trying to be present, feeling the weight of her words. Just then, my phone buzzed. It was my best friend, calling. I picked up, and her voice trembled—she’d just had a huge fight with her partner and needed someone to talk to. She asked if I had a moment. I looked at my mom, who was waiting for comfort, and then at my phone, hearing my friend’s distress. My heart pounded as I realized both needed me right now, but I couldn’t be in two places at once. I felt torn, guilt rising no matter which way I leaned, wishing I could split myself in two.
